items.title: Kennedy Center Sets 2026 Honorees: David Mamet, Paul Anka, Andy Garcia and More
items.summary:
The John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts named Paul Anka, David Foster, Andy Garcia, David Mamet and Barbara Mandrell as the recipients of the 49th Kennedy Center Honors, announcing the class alongside President Donald Trump. The ceremony is set for Dec. 7 and will be held at Capital One Arena, the first time the Honors have taken place outside the center itself.

The announcement arrives months later than usual. As Variety noted, honorees are typically revealed between July and September, and this year the center has neither a host nor a broadcast partner in place. CBS carried the event every year from its 1978 debut, but the network's rights to the telecast expired in 2025.

The delay follows a long fight over the building's name. Trump's handpicked board voted in December 2025 to add his name to the center; a federal judge ruled in May that only Congress can rename it, and the name came down in June. After the judge blocked a second attempt in September, the board voted to close the center, citing structural deterioration, and Trump has said renovations will not begin unless a higher court restores his name, warning the building could otherwise be "ripped down." The Justice Department has argued in support, saying the center faces financial and physical collapse.

The honorees span music, film and theater. Anka wrote "Diana" and "My Way"; Foster has won 16 Grammys and helped launch Celine Dion and Michael Bublé; Garcia drew an Oscar nomination and appeared in "The Godfather: Part III" and "Ocean's Eleven"; Mamet won the Pulitzer Prize and wrote "Glengarry Glen Ross" and "Oleanna"; Mandrell is the country singer behind "(If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to Be Right."

"We are recognizing amazing artists whose lifelong work has shaped American culture and inspired generations of audiences," Trump said in a statement. "We are proud to honor this year's class and to continue a tradition that has defined the Center for nearly 50 years."

Trump hosted the 2025 gala himself, which honored Sylvester Stallone, Gloria Gaynor, George Strait, KISS and Michael Crawford and drew a sharp decline in viewers. Past Honors recipients include Aretha Franklin, Paul McCartney, Meryl Streep, Steven Spielberg, Bruce Springsteen, Dolly Parton, Led Zeppelin and Sidney Poitier. The center has not said who will host or air the December ceremony.

items.title: Bruce Springsteen Endorses Michigan Senate Candidate Abdul El-Sayed: “I’m In His Corner 100%”
items.summary:
Bruce Springsteen endorsed Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed on Monday, posting his support to social media hours before polls opened in the 2026 midterms. El-Sayed, a Democrat, is running against Republican Mike Rogers in a race that has tightened in the closing stretch.

"Dr. El-Sayed is a fighter for our American Constitution, he's a fighter for our American Democracy, and he's a fighter against the corrupt, lawless, and anti-American leadership currently in the White House," Springsteen wrote. "That's why I'm in his corner 100%."

The endorsement is unusual in its specificity. As Deadline noted, Springsteen has campaigned for Barack Obama, Hillary Clinton, Joe Biden and Kamala Harris, but he rarely weighs in this directly on races below the presidential level.

Springsteen has spent the past year putting his politics into the work itself. In January he released "Streets of Minneapolis," written about the killings of Renee Good and Alex Pretti by ICE agents in Minnesota, and he performed the song in that city during his spring tour with the E Street Band. Trump responded by calling the 77-year-old a "very boring singer" who "looks like a dried up prune who has suffered greatly from the work of a really bad plastic surgeon."

Last month Springsteen appeared with Tom Morello at the Power to the People festival in Columbia, Maryland, a daylong protest concert broadcast on MS NOW and streamed online. Over the spring and summer he described the administration from the stage as "reckless and treasonous."

The Michigan race took a turn on Sunday when El-Sayed's former primary opponent, Haley Stevens, endorsed Rogers, a move that drew immediate backlash and cost her standing in her own state party. Democrats are expected to take the House, and control of the Senate could hinge on Michigan and a handful of other contests.

items.title: Sharon Horgan’s ‘Youth’ Renewed For Season 2 At HBO
items.summary:
HBO renewed Sharon Horgan's comedy "Youth" for a second season, confirming the pickup less than a day after the first-season finale aired. Horgan created and wrote the series and stars as Alex, a literary agent navigating her fifties.

The eight-episode season followed Alex, a 50-year-old divorcee, as she looked for sex and love while caring for her ailing parents and managing a son who should be an adult by now. The finale left several threads open: Alex ends her relationship with Patrick, played by Rupert Friend, after finding a pros-and-cons list that files her inability to have children under cons, then sleeps with her nemesis Malcolm, played by Douglas Hodge, and wakes to learn her boss Sam, played by Sharlene Whyte, has signed him as a client. Aran Murphy plays her child Ruari and Robbie Gee plays Sam's husband, Frank.

"I'm so happy to get another opportunity to live out my emotional and biological crises on HBO. I can't think of a better platform to air my UTI problems on," Horgan said in a statement reported by Deadline. "The response to Youth has been beyond what I could have hoped for."

HBO comedy chief Amy Gravitt said the series "makes us howl with laughter and with tears often in the same moment" and praised the ensemble. Horgan's company Merman produces, with Horgan executive producing alongside Faye Dorn, Jim Kleverweis and Dawn Shadforth, who also directs.

The show marks Horgan's return to HBO seven years after "Divorce" wrapped its third season. She co-created "Catastrophe" and is also behind Apple's "Bad Sisters," Starz's "Shining Vale" with Courteney Cox, and the BBC's "Motherland." HBO has not announced a production start or premiere window for the second season.
